answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity commits a hash of its prior-epoch action vector; the next epoch's actions must match within a drift threshold, enforced by replaying stored proofs. Sybil clusters fracture because fresh identities have no matching history, costing attackers a full epoch of genuine, consistent activity per identity—slow like a glacier—before it can transact. Mismatches flag accounts for karst-like erosion of trust weight, and each failed identity burns its accumulated ember of reputation, forcing re-earned history from zero.
